She was primarily diagnosed with neuro-Behcet’s disease, since her father (patient 11) had been diagnosed with Behcet’s disease and she had positive HLA B5 and HLA B51. She was being treated with methylprednisolone pulse and azathioprine. She continued to present episodes of stroke with evidence of hemorrhagic components and vascular nature on MRI. plate_findings.evidence: Caption: sections of skin biopsy from DADA2 patients showing medium-vessel vasculitis with lymphovascular occlusion, inflammatory infiltrates containing neutrophils, and intravascular thrombi.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Real human skin-biopsy histology from a DADA2 patient demonstrating medium-vessel vasculitis. The article title and caption directly attribute the panel findings to DADA2, while the appearance resembles PAN. B: Real human arterial biopsy showing destructive medium-vessel vasculitis in a DADA2 patient. The destructive transmural process directly supports necrotizing small- to medium-vessel vasculitis. C: Human DADA2 skin-biopsy histology showing small-vessel vasculitis. Although interpreted as possible PAN-like vasculitis, the cohort and caption attribute the biopsy to DADA2, so the configured disease assignment is DADA2.
panels.attribution_text: Barron et al. The Spectrum of the Deficiency of Adenosine Deaminase 2: An Observational Analysis of a 60 Patient Cohort.. Frontiers in immunology 2021. doi:10.3389/fimmu.2021.811473. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: The medium vessel vasculitis in DADA2 patients resembles the vasculitis in polyarteritis nodosa. (A) Sections of skin biopsy showing lymphovascular occlusion in medium vessels in the medium-to-deep dermis with inflammatory infiltrate with neutrophils and intravascular thrombi. (B) Vasculitis of a medium sized artery characterized by dense transmural infiltrate of mononuclear cells and neutrophils with karyorrhexis, fibrin deposits in vascular lumen, destruction of vessel walls and dense chronic inflammation surrounding the affected blood vessel. (C) Vasculitis involving smaller blood vessels of the superficial subcutis. This biopsy was interpreted as possible polyarteritis nodosa.
in_text_mentions: g underlying immune deficiency (14). There was a range of skin biopsy findings including lesions showing lymphovascular occlusion in medium vessels with inflammatory infiltrates and intravascular thrombi ( Figure 3A ). Vasculitis of medium-sized arterial vessels that resembled PAN was noted with features of mononuclear cells and neutrophils, karyorrhexis, fibrin deposits in vascular lumens, destruction of vessel walls, and dense chronic inflammation surrounding affected blood vessels ( Figure 3B ). Vasculitis involving smaller blood vessels of the superficial cutis was also seen ( Figure 3C ).

findings.label: Livedo racemosa
findings.evidence: Caption: "mottled, somewhat reticular erythema representing livedo racemosa"

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph of a patient with DADA2 showing a well-defined irregular ulcer with overlying yellow fibrinous exudate; the caption explicitly attributes the skin ulceration to DADA2. The ulceration is not represented in the provided finding vocabulary. B: Clinical photograph shows distal lower-leg mottled reticular erythema explicitly identified as livedo racemosa, a characteristic cutaneous manifestation of DADA2. C: Clinical photograph shows multiple hypopigmented atrophic plaques identified in the caption as scars from prior ulcerations in a patient with DADA2. Scarring is a recognized cutaneous sequela and is not separately represented in the supplied vocabulary.
panels.attribution_text: Barron et al. The Spectrum of the Deficiency of Adenosine Deaminase 2: An Observational Analysis of a 60 Patient Cohort.. Frontiers in immunology 2021. doi:10.3389/fimmu.2021.811473. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 10.
panels.figure_caption: Skin ulceration in DADA2. (A) A 40-year-old developed a well-defined, irregularly shaped ulceration with overlying yellow fibrinous exudate (black arrow). The ulcer was not infected. There had been antecedent trauma 3 months prior with a small skin tear. This lesion developed while on adalimumab and screening for neutralizing antibodies to adalimumab was negative. (B) Distal to the knees there was increasing mottled, somewhat reticular erythema representing livedo racemosa. (C) Further examination revealed multiple hypopigmented atrophic plaques consistent with scars from prior ulcerations (white arrows).
in_text_mentions: • 39-year-old female (Patient 45) with a history of multiple chronic ankle ulcerations ( Figure 10 ) and Raynaud’s phenomenon. Lower DBI waveform and pressure was abnormal in her digits, suggesting small-vessel disease. MRA revealed attenuated appearance of the peroneal artery.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Clinical photograph of livedo racemosa in a patient from a DADA2 cohort; the caption directly identifies this characteristic DADA2 manifestation. B: The panel shows cutaneous nodules in a DADA2 patient, with biopsy described as medium-vessel vasculitis consistent with a cutaneous PAN-like manifestation. [raw subtype: cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa–like vasculitis] C: Clinical photograph of a child's fingers with Raynaud phenomenon, explicitly captioned as a cutaneous manifestation of DADA2. Raynaud phenomenon is absent from the allowed findings vocabulary. D: The caption directly identifies acral cyanosis and a cutaneous ulcer as manifestations of DADA2. These specific terms are not represented in the allowed vocabulary, so they are proposed findings. E: The panel shows periungual wart-like lesions identified in the caption as verruca vulgaris, a DADA2 manifestation attributed by the article to underlying immune deficiency. The...

panels.figure_caption: The cutaneous manifestations of DADA2. (A) Livedo racemosa on the legs of a 38-year-old. (B) Nodules that when biopsied revealed medium vessel vasculitis in a 58-year-old. (Cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa [PAN]). (C) Raynaud’s phenomenon in a 13-month-old. (D) Acral cyanosis and cutaneous ulcer in a 27-year-old. (E) Verruca vulgaris in a 29-year-old.
in_text_mentions: Skin involvement was the most common manifestation seen in this cohort and was observed in 52/58 patients (90%), with livedo racemosa present in 43/58 patients (74%) ( Figure 2A ). A history of cutaneous features resembling polyarteritis nodosa (PAN)/nodules was noted in 33/58 patients (57%) ( Figure 2B ) and Raynaud’s phenomena was seen in 13/58 patients (22%) ( Figure 2C ). Skin ulcerations were found in 3 patients ( Figure 2D ). Verrucae vulgaris (warts) were seen in 11/58 patients (19%) ( Figure 2E ), likely reflecting underlying immune deficiency (14). panels.rationale: Clinical photograph clearly demonstrating livedo racemosa (reticulated skin discoloration) on the lower limb of a patient with DADA2. The caption explicitly identifies the finding and the article title confirms the disease association. No third-party attribution is present.

panels.figure_caption: Livedo racemosa noted on both lower limbs
in_text_mentions: At the acute presentation, he was afebrile and haemodynamically stable. Systemic examination including full neurological examination was normal except for livedo racemosa on his lower limbs (Fig. 1). He was also noted to have a mildly swollen and tender right testicle, but without typical clinical features of torsion. Repeat laboratory workup revealed a normal full blood count (haemoglobin 125 g/L; total white cell count 6.56 X109/L [RR 5–15]; platelets 306 X109/L [RR150–450]); normal liver, renal and coagulation profile. ESR was mildly elevated at 28 mm/hr. [RR < 10]; CRP of 17 mg/L [RR < 20]

findings.label: Necrotizing small- to medium-vessel vasculitis
findings.evidence: small-vessel vasculitis consistent with inflammatory infiltrates surrounding them

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (2a, 2b, 2c). 2a: H&E histology from the ulcer biopsy of a DADA2 patient showing vessel wall thickening, fibrosis, and thrombus occluding the lumen. 2b: H&E section from the DADA2 patient's ulcer biopsy showing small-vessel vasculitis with inflammatory infiltrates surrounding vessels. 2c: H&E section from the same DADA2 ulcer biopsy showing interstitial accumulation of neutrophils and eosinophils along with fibrosis.
panels.attribution_text: Contractor et al. A Rare Genetic Mutation Leading to a Deficiency of Adenosine Deaminase 2 Enzyme in a Long-Standing Case of Cutaneous Polyarteritis Nodosa: A Case Report.. Cureus 2022. doi:10.7759/cureus.30295. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathology slides of the ulcer biopsy with hematoxylin and eosin staining. (a) (40× magnification) (A) vessel wall thickening and fibrosis, and (B) thrombus occluding the lumen. (b) (20× magnification) small-vessel vasculitis consistent with inflammatory infiltrates surrounding them. (c) (20× magnification) shows the interstitial accumulation of neutrophils and eosinophils along with fibrosis.
in_text_mentions: A biopsy of the skin lesion in the left lower leg was collected and sent for histopathology. It showed intimal vessel proliferation and thickening seen along with thrombosis (Figures 2a, 2b) leading to Ischemia and ulceration. In addition, it showed an infiltrate mixed with neutrophils and eosinophils in and around the vessels involving the panniculus causing panniculitis (Figure 3a) and blood vessels filled with neutrophilic infiltrate and recanalization consistent with healed vasculitis (Figure 3b).
